## WF1 ONBOARDING NOTIFY v1.0

**Setup: one value and one credential.**

1. `Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)` -> select a **Google Service Account** credential.
   That is the only thing to set. The document ID and tab name are literals on that node.
2. Share the sheet with the service account email address, as Editor.
3. The sheet needs a tab named `Onboarding_Audit` with these headers in row 1:

`contractor_id | timestamp | outcome | correlation_id | event_kind | contract_type | agency_name | email_state | sms_state | demo_mode`

A service account is used rather than OAuth2 because this n8n runs on plain HTTP,
and Google only accepts HTTPS redirect URIs. A service account is also the right
choice for an unattended production workflow: it belongs to the system, not to a
person whose token dies when they leave.

Both notification channels point at a public echo endpoint that returns the request
body, so the email content is visible in the execution log without any key.

**Test payloads**

Happy path -> `documents_verified: true`
Chase path -> `documents_verified: false`
Validation -> omit `contract_type`, or send `documents_verified: "false"` as a string
Malformed  -> post `{"contractor_id":` with Content-Type application/json
Duplicate  -> post the happy path payload twice

**IMPORTANT:** n8n only persists workflow static data on PRODUCTION executions.
Activate the workflow and use the production webhook URL, or the duplicate
suppression demo will not work.

**Security note.** The webhook is left unauthenticated so this can be imported and
tested immediately. In production it would take Header Auth plus an IP allowlist,
and the stub URLs would be SendGrid and Respond.io behind stored credentials.

## Design decisions

**Validation is one Code node, not an IF chain.** Eight IF nodes report one failure at
a time. This collects every problem into one array so a caller fixes the payload in a
single round trip. It returns instead of throwing, so a bad payload can never crash
the run.

**`documents_verified` must be a real boolean.** The string `"false"` is truthy in
JavaScript. Accepting it would route an unverified contractor down the welcome branch.
That is the kind of quiet integration bug that only shows up in a complaint.

**Idempotency before send, not after.** The key is contractor + agency + start date +
event kind. Static data keeps this dependency free. Its limit is stated in the node
itself: it is not a distributed lock, and in production it becomes an atomic claim in
SQL Server. If nothing was delivered the claim is released, so a genuine retry is
never blocked by a send that did not happen.

**Multi-channel with real fallback.** Email carries the detail, SMS is the nudge. Both
are always attempted and scored independently, so if email is rejected the contractor
is still reached and the response says `207` rather than pretending it was clean.

## Honest scope and what Workflow 2 adds

**2xx means accepted, not delivered.** Every channel outcome is `accepted`,
`rejected`, `uncertain` or `not_attempted`. 5xx and transport failures are
deliberately `uncertain`, because the provider may or may not have sent the message,
and calling that a success is how a missed notification becomes invisible.

**Every external call has both outputs wired.** Nothing reaches a dead end and no
failure is swallowed. The audit row is written on all three paths, including
validation failures, so the sheet is a complete record of what arrived, not just of
what worked.

**Sheets writes use cell format RAW.** A contractor ID beginning with `=` cannot
become a live formula in the audit sheet.

**Where malformed JSON is actually caught.** If a caller declares
`Content-Type: application/json` and sends invalid JSON, n8n's own HTTP layer rejects
it before any node runs and returns its own structured JSON error. No node can catch
that, and nothing is half-processed. If the body arrives as text, Raw Body hands it to
`Validate and Normalise`, which catches the parse failure and returns this workflow's
own 400 `invalid_json`. Both routes are graceful; they are simply owned by different
components, and it is worth knowing which is which.

**Deliberately NOT in this workflow:** automatic send retries, exhausted-retry
alerting, and dead lettering. Those are Workflow 2, built as a separate workflow so the
retry and alerting pattern is reusable rather than welded into onboarding.
